articles.title: Thailand welcomes US-Myanmar engagement, expects ASEAN talks on country’s future - WTVB
articles.summary: Thailand welcomes US-Myanmar engagement, expects ASEAN talks on country’s future  WTVB
articles.full_text:
By Sergio Goncalves and Miguel Pereira
LISBON, Oct 23 (Reuters) – Thailand welcomes US engagement with Myanmar and expects discussions at the Association of Southeast Asian Nations’ November summit in Manila on how to proceed with the member barred since the 2021 coup, Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow told Reuters on Friday.
The United States and Myanmar’s military-backed government held talks in Tokyo two weeks ago, their second meeting in a month as Washington steps up re-engagement with the generals it shunned after the coup.
“We don’t want to see Myanmar isolated, we don’t want Myanmar to be an arena for geopolitical rivalry … so the US engagement is something that we welcome,” he said.
Engagement “does not mean legitimizing the regime,” but aims to encourage peaceful conflict resolution and reconciliation with the opposition, Sihasak, who is also deputy prime minister, added.
He said there was “some shift in ASEAN’s position,” citing Myanmar President Min Aung Hlaing’s recent visits to Laos, Cambodia, Vietnam, Thailand and Malaysia, but said it was unclear whether the Manila summit would address restoring Myanmar’s full representation.
“It’s good that we’re going to have a very substantive, very extensive, and very in-depth discussion on how to proceed on Myanmar,” he said.
He also said Thailand and Cambodia could resolve their longstanding land and maritime boundary disputes within 12 to 18 months despite limited progress.
“It is possible, everything is possible,” he said, cautioning that confidence-building and addressing security concerns along the land border, where clashes have occurred, must come first.
Cambodia launched a conciliation process under the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea in June to resolve the maritime boundary dispute, after Thailand terminated a 2001 joint development framework in May following deadly border clashes. The first meeting was held about a month ago.
“Right now, we haven’t achieved, to be very frank, much progress,” he said.
The maritime dispute centers on overlapping claims to about 26,000 sq km in the Gulf of Thailand, believed to hold oil and gas reserves worth around $300 billion. Thailand wants the boundary defined before discussing resource-sharing, he said.
Thailand-EU free-trade talks are in their final stage and could conclude by year-end if there is mutual political will, he added.
(Reporting by Sergio Goncalves and Miguel Pereira in Lisbon; Editing by Matthew Lewis)

articles.summary: Want to escape the haze in Malaysia? Here are some clean air havens you can visit  The Straits TimesTSH Resources reports 274 hot spots within estate boundaries after SGX queries over haze  The Business TimesMalaysia keeps Indonesia firefighting aid offer open, no local companies linked to forest fires  AsiaOne.comCan ASEAN enforce its way out of the haze crisis?  East Asia ForumHaze: Expedite enactment of comprehensive Clean Air Act, says Lee Lam Thye&nbs...
articles.full_text:
AI generated
KUALA LUMPUR – With the prospect of haze enveloping some of Singaporeans’ favourite Malaysian travel destinations like Kuala Lumpur and Johor Bahru, those who want to enjoy a ringgit holiday can still visit spots with a record of cleaner air ahead of the upcoming school holidays.
While experts say it is difficult to accurately predict how the winds will blow beyond the next five days even with forecasting tools, data shows that parts of east Malaysia and some states in the north, like Perlis, Kedah and Kelantan, have been enjoying good air quality for the past fortnight.
Based on Malaysia’s Air Pollutant Index (API), where a reading below 100 is deemed safe for outdoor activities, these states have registered readings hovering around 50. In contrast, API readings in places like Kuala Lumpur average above 150.
With regular appearances on the Department of Environment’s daily rankings for locations with the lowest API readings across Malaysia, here are three places to go where the sky is blue and your dollar can be stretched.
Langkawi (Average API: 30s; Good air quality)
Called the Jewel of Kedah, Langkawi comprises a group of islands off the west coast of northern Malaysia. Its average API level in the past week is in the 30s.
“The air here is superb,” said Wendy Chin, a licensed nature guide who leads birding and kayaking tours on the island.
She recommends that visitors explore natural outdoor and recreational spots. “Tourists with a budget can go for mangrove tours, those with a limited budget can visit waterfalls and lepak,” she added, using the Malay slang for “chilling out”.

Langkawi is home to the UNESCO-listed Kilim Karst Geoforest Park and a few waterfalls, including the Seven Wells Waterfall, named after seven natural freshwater pools that resemble stone wells.
Other landmarks include the 125m-long curved suspension Sky Bridge offering views of rainforests and the Andaman Sea, as well as Cenang Beach and Dayang Bunting Island, which has a silhouette resembling a pregnant maiden.
A travel planner at My Curious Trips, who wanted to be known only as Yannick, said Langkawi offers a mix of nature, beaches, shopping and good food such as crab noodles.
Another pull factor is duty-free products like alcohol, imported chocolates and perfumes that are cheaper than on the mainland.
Balik Pulau (API: 40s; Good)
Penang is no stranger to many Singaporeans, who can likely rattle off names like Armenian Street, Batu Ferringhi and Cheong Fatt Tze Mansion like their ABCs. But it is the Balik Pulau region in the west of the island that enjoyed the cleanest air in Penang in October, with an average API reading in the mid-40s.
Balik Pulau – “the back of the island” in Malay – is located about 20km from George Town and is most conveniently accessible by car. Drivers can get there via a coastal route with beach views, or through a mountain pass with lush forests.
For those who brave the journey, Balik Pulau’s eco-tourism offers a different experience from the heritage of George Town, said Penang’s tourism and creative economy committee chairman Wong Hon Wai.
He added that Balik Pulau is especially popular during the durian season, as it is known as Penang’s durian heartland. Apart from the thorny fruit, Balik Pulau is also home to the Ghee Hup Nutmeg Factory, where visitors can sample the fruit in its jam, pickled or juice variants.
On a day with good weather, tourists can explore mangrove reserves by boat or cycle around the countryside, exploring paddy fields and fruit orchards, before ending the night with a seafood dinner.
Kota Kinabalu (API: 50s; Moderate)
Even though Sabah’s capital experienced transboundary haze earlier in September, the situation has improved significantly and its latest API readings hovered in the low 50s.
As blue skies and fresh air are in abundance in Kota Kinabalu, tourists can take their pick between nature and cultural day trips to the Mari Mari Cultural Village or Tunku Abdul Rahman Marine Park.
Water activities like stand-up paddle boarding, hydrofoil surfing and parasailing against the Borneo sunset are available at the popular Tanjung Aru beach.
Unclouded skies may also open the door to early morning drives to see Malaysia’s tallest peak Mount Kinabalu from spots like the ticketed Kinabalu Park or the Pekan Nabalu lookout point. However, the end of the year may bring rain, which makes climbing the mountain less advisable.
For now, the clear air has already been restorative for some travellers.
Walking across Tanjung Aru Beach, a popular sunset spot, online advertisement executive Delphine Tan, 39, said the air in Kota Kinabalu was much better than in Kuala Lumpur. She was on a trip with her husband to visit the beaches and mountain town Kundasang, which is near Mount Kinabalu.
She told ST: “My sinusitis has not flared up here. The sunshine is nice and the air quality is good.”
- Additional reporting by Hazlin Hassan and Lu Wei Hoong

articles.title: UEF welcomed Consulate General of Indonesia in HCMC, widening perspective on ASEAN economic strategy - UEF
articles.summary: UEF welcomed Consulate General of Indonesia in HCMC, widening perspective on ASEAN economic strategy  UEF
articles.full_text:
The Faculty of International Relations always places emphasis on strengthening connections with diplomatic missions and introducing international perspectives to teaching and learning activities. Building on that direction, the faculty held a ceremony to welcome Ms. Carolina Tinangon, Consul General of the Republic of Indonesia in Ho Chi Minh, and organized the seminar “Foreign Direct Investment and Strategic Economic Security in ASEAN.”
The seminar allowed students to directly discuss with high representatives and widen their practical perspectives on international relations
Attending the event were Dr. Do Huu Nguyen Loc, Vice President; Dr. Tran My Hai Loc, Deputy Dean of the Faculty of International Relations; and many lecturers and students interested in the topic.
The support from the Consulate General of the Republic of Indonesia in HCMC demonstrates the Faculty’s direction to connect with diplomatic missions
Focusing on current regional economic and strategic issues, the seminar provided an academic platform for students to explore high representatives’ perspectives and enrich their viewpoints on issues in the international relations field. Instead of only learning from documents and lectures, they had the opportunity to ask questions directly, listen to the speaker’s insights, and proactively connect specialized knowledge with practice.
The seminar’s content closely relates to a wide range of modules in the curriculum, such as International Political Economy, Sociology, Sea Power, and Diplomatic Practice. The combination of these topics encouraged students to develop multidimensional thinking, critical thinking, argumentation skills, and academic communication skills. This skill package is particularly necessary for learners to develop their professional competence and adapt to the requirements of the International Relations field.
Ms. Carolina Tinangon introduced practical perspectives in the field of International Relations
The seminar is the highlight of the activity series “Diplomat's Talks,” organized as part of the 10th anniversary celebration of the Faculty of International Relations at UEF. By connecting with diplomatic missions and integrating practical topics into teaching and learning activities, the Faculty provides students with opportunities to gain exposure to international environments as well as to enhance their autonomy in learning and career development while they are still students.
UEFers confidently discussed and raised questions to gain more knowledge
Furthermore, support from the Consulate General of the Republic of Indonesia helped strengthen the connection between diplomatic activities and higher education. This also demonstrates UEF and the Faculty of International Relations’ efforts to promote international cooperation and enhance the practicality of the study programs, which affirms their credibility throughout the development journey.

articles.title: Myanmar: Multidimensional Challenges Continue Amidst Outreach to ASEAN - Security Risks Asia
articles.summary: Myanmar: Multidimensional Challenges Continue Amidst Outreach to ASEAN  Security Risks Asia
articles.full_text:
The Union Government’s military led administration is strengthening the nominally civilian posture even as a parallel consolidation is ongoing by the alternative Spring Revolution forces led by the Steering Council for the Emergence of a Federal Democratic Union (SCEF). While the Union government is focusing on the main cities as Yangon and Mandalay the SCEF is dominant in the rural zones. Active conflicts are persisting across multiple states. Armed opposition groups and ethnic resistance organizations continue localized pressure, where the central administration faces ongoing challenges regarding territorial control. Intense fighting is ongoing in the Rakhine and the Chin States presumably as the President is keen to fulfil assurances given to China and India to open up the trade routes. The Union Government also focused on managing regional relations within the broader framework of ASEAN and neighbouring bilateral partners, attempting to secure diplomatic recognition. The SCEF’s attempts at international outreach remain weak. The economy is no longer experiencing collapse seen immediately after the coup period, growth remains low, inflation remains among the highest in Southeast Asia, and conflict continues to constrain productivity and investment.
International Relations
United States.
United States and Myanmar's Union government held talks in Tokyo in the second meeting in a month as Washington steps up re-engagement as per Reuters.
Talks in Myanmar's capital Naypyitaw in mid-September had focused on securing the release of an American businessman Adam Castillo, a former head of the American Chamber of Commerce in Myanmar and shutting down scam centres that target Americans.
US Assistant Secretary of State for Intelligence and Research Michael Vance led the talks in Tokyo talks.
Vance has previously met the democratic opposition and ethnic armed organizations fighting the military, both in person and online.
The US explained lifting of sanctions on the daughter of a Myanmar businessman accused of supporting the country's military, saying the move was part of a new approach to the country as one of the range of tools employed to gain recognition.
Against this background it is seen that the U.
S.
has however not offered recognition, sanctions relief, or formal agreements on minerals or scam centre crackdowns.
Current outreach is narrow, unscheduled, and lacks a published negotiating mandate.
Possibility of success is modest: the junta may cooperate tactically on scam centres to gain diplomatic space, but deeper collaboration on rare earths risks conferring de facto recognition—something Washington has avoided.
Moreover the rare-earth deposits Washington is interested in lie mainly in territory held by the Kachin Independence Army (KIA) in Kachin State which are difficult to retrieve.

China. As the US resumed direct engagement with Myanmar’s Union Government, Beijing moved to cement its overarching influence by meeting with nine political parties in Yangon to gauge public sentiment. The Chinese delegation was led by Peng Xiubin, director‑general of the Chinese Communist Party’s International Liaison Department. Beijing also maintains influence over the Kachin Independence Army, which controls key mines, ensuring continued preferential access and complicating U.S. entry.
Spring Revolution Forces. CRPH said on 12 October that the 153rd Assembly of the Inter-Parliamentary Union [IPU], held in Arusha, Tanzania on 9 October had adopted a resolution to continue recognizing the CRPH as a key partner for dialogue for a fifth consecutive year, granting its delegation non-voting observer status while refusing to recognize the military-backed parliament, and addressing the situation of Myanmar’s elected parliamentarians who remain unlawfully detained. A delegation from the Steering Council for the Emergence of a Federal Democratic Union (SCEF) met with Australian Foreign Minister Penny Wong at Parliament House in Canberra, Australia, on 28 September, according to a statement released by SCEF 1 October.
Regional Relations
ASEAN. The Union Government led by President and former Tatmadaw Chief Senior General Min Aung Hlaing is striving to gain recognition and reintegrate with the ASEAN. In October, Malaysia was Min Aung Hlaing’s fifth stop to an ASEAN member after Thailand, Laos, Cambodia, Vietnam collectively enhancing his political standing. Repatriation of Myanmar nationals from Malaysia dominated talks between Myanmar Union Government President Min Aung Hlaing and Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim during visit of the Myanmar leader to Kuala Lumpur. This comes as on September 29, Malaysian authorities sent back 1,476 Myanmar nationals—1,370 men, 79 women, 20 boys, and 7 girls, ages 8 to 60, aboard two Myanmar navy ships and a hospital ship from Lumut naval base in Malaysia’s Perak state. The deportations come amid a wave of public hostility in Malaysia toward refugees, particularly Rohingya, that government officials have fomented.
Malaysia’s reception of Min Aung Hlaing, coupled with pledges to work toward Myanmar’s “full reintegration into ASEAN,” marks the strongest signal of regional re engagement. The Philippines, as ASEAN Chair. President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. hailed recent visits by Myanmar coup leader Min Aung Hlaing to ASEAN countries as part of a “new approach” to resolving the country’s crisis. To effect integration the Union Government has appointed ASEAN Affairs Committee to lobby remaining skeptical members. ASEAN’s Five-Point Consensus consists of ending violence, beginning dialogue among all parties, appointing an ASEAN special envoy, and ensuring that humanitarian assistance those in need is now under stress. The consensus will have little practical value if their conditions are repeatedly affirmed in statements but lose influence in diplomatic practice. Thus, performative nonrecognition by the ASEAN as well as international community at large and more particularly by Asian countries is evident in Myanmar.
Suu Kyi and Reintegration. Publishing of pictures of Daw Aung Suu Kyi receiving packages from Britain’s King Charles III and allowing Kim Aris son of the Nobel lauraeate the first telephonic conversation with the octogenarian leader for the first time in five years is a calibrated political signal: the regime is showcasing controlled access to Suu Kyi to project normalcy, counter “proof of life” pressure, and seek international legitimacy amid deepening civil war. The timing—days after releasing images of Suu Kyi receiving books and a letter from King Charles III—suggests an orchestrated campaign to soften the junta’s pariah status and extract diplomatic concessions. However, having described her as as ‘special female prisoner,’ the waters may be muddied. Nevertheless, states acting in national interest would be willing to engage with the Union Government with an opening by the US is also visible to Government
India. Attempts to reopen the promised trade routes to India are ongoing with progress made in the Chin State where a four-pronged offensive is ongoing. The Myanmar Policy Institute’s latest report for October examines the implementation of the India–Myanmar–Thailand (IMT) Trilateral Highway between June and September 2026. MPI report concludes that escalating armed conflict, contested territorial control, damaged infrastructure and the humanitarian consequences of military operations make the full restoration of the highway unlikely in the future.
SCEF Low Diplomatic Heft. The main opposition political grouping Steering Council for the Emergence of a Federal Democratic Union (SCEF) and other resistance actors will need to demonstrate effective governance in territories they administer, strengthen civilian protection against air attacks, and develop credible cooperation with foreign governments on shared concerns such as online scams, transnational crime, trade and regional security to gain a degree of recognition.
Political Developments
Myanmar Union Parliament on 18 October extended a state of emergency in 55 townships for another 90 days, as lawmakers supporting the move conceded that administration and the rule of law had yet to return to normal across the affected areas. The townships lie in Sagaing and Magway regions and in Chin, Rakhine, Karenni, Karen and Shan states. Ngazun Township in Mandalay Region and Kyaukme and Hsipaw townships in northern Shan State were dropped from the list. The list has shrunk slowly from 63 townships on 31 July 2025 to 55 townships now
The Steering Council for the Emergence of a Federal Democratic Union (SCEF) is continuing with online meetings with political organisations such as the New Mon State Party–Anti-Dictatorship (NMSP-AD), Mon State Federal Council (MSFC), Mon State Consultative Council (MSCC) and Committee Representing Mon State Hluttaw (CRMH). SCEF’s legitimacy inside Myanmar is growing but uneven, rooted in its coalition of major Ethnic Armed Organizations (KIO, KNU, KNPP, CNF), the NUG, and CRPH — a grouping now seen as the most structured resistance authority since 2021. Its three pillar design (ERO/federal units, people’s representatives, women’s representatives) and rapid outreach to PDFs and local administrations give it procedural legitimacy among resistance constituencies, especially in Sagaing, Kachin, Karen, Chin, and Karenni areas. This reflects an emerging federal power sharing framework rather than ad hoc coordination. To integrate all allied forces within Karenni State into a unified defense structure, the Karenni State Interim Council (IEC) announced that the Karenni State Interim Parliament enacted a unified Karenni Military Law on October 21.

Intense fighting is ongoing in multiple provinces and states to include Tanintharyi Region, multiple townships in Sagaing Region, Kachin State, Magwe Region Myaing Township which is an oil hub, Mon State and Karenni State amongst others.

articles.title: Inaugural Invest Malaysia Day 2026 Highlights How Singapore Businesses Can Tap Malaysia's Next Phase of Growth - PR Newswire
articles.summary: Inaugural Invest Malaysia Day 2026 Highlights How Singapore Businesses Can Tap Malaysia's Next Phase of Growth  PR Newswire
articles.full_text:
- Malaysian Investment Development Authority (MIDA), Singapore Business Federation (SBF) and CIMB Singapore convened businesses and investors in Singapore to explore opportunities across Malaysia's high-growth sectors while fostering dialogue on regional expansion and Singapore-Malaysia business opportunities.
SINGAPORE, Oct. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Building on its longstanding collaboration, Malaysian Investment Development Authority (MIDA), Singapore Business Federation (SBF) and CIMB Singapore yesterday concluded the inaugural Invest Malaysia Day 2026 in Singapore, bringing together over 200 businesses and investors in Singapore to explore investment insights, business advisory support and partnership opportunities across Malaysia. The forum underscored the growing importance of the Singapore-Malaysia economic relationship, connecting attendees with representatives from Malaysia's federal investment agencies, regional development authorities and ecosystem partners.
The forum was officiated by Guest-of-Honour Her Excellency Datin Paduka Anizan Siti Hajjar Adnin, High Commissioner of Malaysia to Singapore, who delivered the keynote address. Keynote addresses were also delivered by Malaysian state investment leaders YB Tuan Ng Sze Han of Selangor, YB Lee Ting Han of Johor and YB Dato' Mohamad Nizar bin Dato' Sri Mohamad Najib of Pahang. Mr. Lee Yee Fung of the Singapore Business Federation and Mr. Benjamin Tan of CIMB Singapore also addressed the participants.
"Malaysia offers Singapore businesses opportunities across diverse growth sectors, supported by well-established industrial ecosystems and strong regional connectivity. National initiatives such as the New Industrial Master Plan (NIMP) 2030, the National Energy Transition Roadmap (NETR) and the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ) provide further avenues for investment across manufacturing, the digital economy, logistics, renewable energy, healthcare and advanced technologies.
As companies assess their next phase of growth, MIDA is committed to helping investors identify suitable locations, understand the regulatory and incentives landscape, and connect with the relevant federal and state agencies. Through this coordinated approach, we aim to facilitate investment decisions and support businesses in establishing and expanding their operations in Malaysia," said Datuk Sikh Shamsul Ibrahim Sikh Abdul Majid, Chief Executive Officer of MIDA.
The day's programme covered:
- A briefing by MIDA on Malaysia's evolving business landscape, priority growth sectors and the incentives, grants and investor support available to companies exploring expansion into Malaysia;
- Insights from state investment leaders on the latest investment developments and economic priorities in Selangor, Johor and Pahang;
- A session on Malaysia's sustainable transition by Ms. Luanne Sieh, Group Chief Sustainability Officer, CIMB, who shared insights on how businesses can position themselves for success by proactively navigating evolving sustainability requirements, leveraging renewable energy options and incentives, and capturing opportunities arising from the country's green transformation agenda;
- A panel discussion on why Malaysia continues to be a preferred investment destination for Singapore businesses, moderated by Mr. Tan Teck Lee, Country Head (Malaysia, Thailand and the Philippines), SBF, with panellists from MIDA, the Malaysian Immigration Department, the Ministry of Human Resources, Knight Frank Malaysia and CIMB Singapore; and
- Parallel state breakout tracks in the afternoon, with Selangor, Pahang, Sarawak and Johor presenting sector-specific opportunities and facilitation support.
"Singapore and Malaysia share one of ASEAN's most interconnected economic partnerships, underpinned by deep trade, investment and business links. As Singapore prepares to assume the ASEAN Chairmanship next year, strengthening these connections will be key to unlocking new opportunities across the region," said Mr. Benjamin Tan, Head of Commercial and Transaction Banking, CIMB Singapore. "As part of a leading ASEAN bank group, CIMB Singapore is committed to supporting businesses in navigating cross-border opportunities and achieve their regional growth ambitions."
"Malaysia remains one of the most compelling growth markets for Singapore businesses, offering a unique combination of strategic location, strong infrastructure, a skilled workforce, and clear government support for investment. Through Invest Malaysia Day 2026, SBF is supporting companies at every stage of their Malaysia journey – from exploration to expansion – with direct access to the federal and state agencies, financial partners, and industry players," said Mr. Lee Yee Fung, Chief Internationalisation & Chief Smart Enterprise Officer, Singapore Business Federation.
Alongside the conference programme, 10 exhibitors consisting of state government agencies and industrial park developers showcased investment opportunities and business support available across Malaysia, giving attendees direct access to investment agencies, state representatives, developers and ecosystem partners to discuss market-entry and expansion plans.
The strong engagement at Invest Malaysia Day 2026 reflects growing confidence in Malaysia's economic outlook and reinforces the importance of closer Singapore-Malaysia collaboration in driving regional growth and competitiveness.
About CIMB
CIMB is one of ASEAN's leading banking groups and Malaysia's second largest financial services provider, by assets. Listed on Bursa Malaysia via CIMB Group Holdings Berhad, it had a market capitalisation of approximately RM80.1 billion as at 30 June 2026. It offers consumer banking, commercial banking, wholesale banking, transaction banking, Islamic banking and asset management products and services. Headquartered in Kuala Lumpur, the Group is present across ASEAN in Malaysia, Indonesia, Singapore, Thailand, Cambodia, Vietnam and the Philippines. Singapore is one of its key markets with approximately 1,000 employees serving clients across consumer, commercial, wholesale and transaction banking products and services.
Beyond ASEAN, the Group has market presence in mainland China, Hong Kong SAR and UK. CIMB has one of the most extensive retail branch networks in ASEAN with 524 branches and over 33,000 employees as at 30 June 2026. CIMB's investment banking arm is one of the largest Asia Pacific-based investment banks, which together with its award-winning treasury & markets and corporate banking units comprise the Group's leading wholesale banking franchise. CIMB is also the 92.46% shareholder of Bank CIMB Niaga in Indonesia, and 94.83% shareholder of CIMB Thai in Thailand.
Sustainability is a core pillar of CIMB's Forward30 strategy and 2030 roadmap. The Group is guided by its Green, Social, Sustainable Impact Products and Services ("GSSIPS") framework, an internal taxonomy designed to deliver impactful sustainable finance. Since launching its sustainable finance framework in 2021, CIMB has progressively raised its ambitions, increasing its initial RM30 billion target to RM100 billion for 2021–2024. The Group now targets RM300 billion in sustainable finance by 2030, reinforcing its commitment to enabling a lower-carbon and more inclusive economy across the region.
About MIDA
MIDA is the government's principal investment promotion and development agency under the Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry (MITI) to oversee and drive investments into the manufacturing and services sectors in Malaysia. Headquartered in Kuala Lumpur Sentral, MIDA has 12 regional and 20 overseas offices. MIDA partners with investors at every stage of their journey, supporting sustainable growth and long-term value creation for Malaysia. For more information, please visit www.mida.gov.my/ and follow MIDA on X, Instagram, Facebook, LinkedIn, TikTok and YouTube.
About Singapore Business Federation
Singapore Business Federation (SBF) is the apex business chamber with over 34,000 members across diverse industries. With a vision to advance Singapore towards a globally competitive and sustainable economy, SBF mobilises the business community to be future-ready and magnify transformation opportunities through policy advocacy, partnership platforms and capability programmes.
For more information, visit www.sbf.org.sg

articles.full_text:
On October 15, 2026, in Panama, the Vietnamese Trade Office in Mexico (also covering Panama) organized a Vietnam-Panama Trade Promotion Seminar. Attendees and speakers included Ms. Phan Thi Nga, representative of the Vietnamese Trade Office in Mexico (also covering Panama); Mr. Hardeep Singh Bhullar, Director of the Foreign Direct Investment Promotion Department, Ministry of Commerce and Industry of Panama (MICI); Ms. Regina Arauz Liakópulos, Honorary Consul of Vietnam in Panama; representatives from the Directorate General of Export Processing Zones/Foreign Trade Zones of Panama; the Director General of the Panamanian Investment Services Directorate; Mr. Servio Samudio, former Ambassador of Panama to Vietnam; and 30 representatives from Panamanian businesses and business associations.
Vietnam-Panama Trade Promotion Workshop: Expanding Opportunities for Trade, Investment, and Logistics Cooperation
The seminar, organized by the Vietnamese Trade Office in Mexico (also covering Panama), was held on October 15, 2026, in Panama City, with the participation of the Panamanian Ministry of Commerce and Industry (MICI). Its aim was to introduce Vietnam's economic and trade potential and connect businesses from both countries, following the official visit of the President of Panama to Vietnam.
In his opening remarks, the representative of the Vietnamese Trade Office in Mexico stated that the seminar was organized to introduce Vietnamese products to Panamanian businesses, helping them find suppliers and partners in Vietnam, and creating more trade and investment opportunities between the two countries. According to the representative of the Vietnamese Trade Office in Mexico, the seminar follows the official visit of Panamanian President José Raúl Mulino to Vietnam in early October 2026, the highest-level visit from Panama to Vietnam in 14 years. The visit yielded many important results: the two governments signed nine cooperation documents; identified priority areas including maritime, aviation, logistics - warehousing, insurance, agriculture , and trade; and agreed to initiate negotiations on an Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement. At the business forum in Hanoi, the President of Panama noted that Panama is entering the largest investment cycle of the century, with Vietnam producing goods and Panama connecting markets, facilitating the global flow of goods.
Regarding economic and trade relations, bilateral trade turnover increased from approximately US$5 million in 2005 to US$478 million in 2025. Of this, Vietnam exported approximately US$462 million to Panama and imported approximately US$15.5 million, indicating significant room for improvement in the trade balance. Ms. Nga also provided an overview of Vietnam's economy: GDP growth in the first nine months of 2026 is projected at approximately 9%; the population is around 103 million; and Vietnam currently has 17 free trade agreements with 60 economies. Although the two countries do not yet have a free trade agreement, Panama recognized Vietnam as a market economy in 2010, and they have agreements on visa exemption and double taxation avoidance.
The Vietnamese Trade Representative in Mexico emphasized the highly complementary nature of the two economies: Vietnam can serve as a bridge for Panama to access Asian markets, while Panama can help Vietnamese businesses connect with Latin American markets. Priority areas for cooperation include agriculture and fisheries (fruits, vegetables, seafood, rice), manufacturing, semiconductors, tourism, and investment. Currently, Panama has 14 investment projects in Vietnam. The Vietnamese Trade Representative in Mexico stated that the two governments have discussed the possibility of Vietnam reopening its embassy in Panama soon, and the Trade Representative hopes to do so at the same time. Panamanian businesses have also been invited to participate in the Vietnam International Sourcing program organized by the Vietnamese Ministry of Industry and Trade, scheduled for July 2027.
On the Panamanian side, Mr. Hardeep Singh Bhullar stated that Panama holds the position of "hub of hubs," boasting a network of over 23 free trade agreements and actively attracting foreign investment. He affirmed that the Panamanian Ministry of Commerce and Industry is ready to support investors and hopes that Vietnamese businesses will explore and invest in Panama. Ms. Regina Arauz Liakópulos, Honorary Consul of Vietnam in Panama, suggested that in addition to trade, it is necessary to strengthen cultural and people-to-people connections between the two countries; she also informed that the Panama Book Fair is expected to invite Vietnam as a guest country.
At the seminar, representatives from the Panamanian Ministry of Commerce and Industry introduced two investment attraction policies. Firstly, the Free Trade Zone regime under Law 32/2011: Panama currently has 27 zones (20 operational, 7 under development) with over 200 businesses; businesses entering these zones do not require a minimum capital investment, licenses are free and unlimited, with a maximum license duration of 90 days; they are exempt from import duties on raw materials and machinery, income tax on exports, and ITBMS (VAT 7%); owners and shareholders are granted permanent residency from the outset. Secondly, there is the Qualified Investor Program: investors are granted permanent residency immediately upon approval, a process that takes approximately 60 days, with a minimum investment of $300,000 (first-time real estate sale), $500,000 (secondary real estate, state bank deposits, securities) or $750,000 (private bank deposits). According to the Panamanian Ministry of Commerce and Industry, the program has been operating for six years, attracting over 900 investors with a total capital exceeding $430 million.
During the discussion, delegates focused on post-licensing procedures, rules of origin, and traceability requirements for goods imported from Vietnam and re-exported to the US market. Representatives from the Panama Chamber of Commerce suggested that attracting Vietnamese investment should be linked to actual suppliers in Panama and industries with local raw materials, such as seafood processing. Panama affirmed its commitment to supporting investors and coordinating with the Vietnamese Trade Office to address any issues; the determination of the conversion rate required for goods to qualify as originating from Panama needs to be considered on a case-by-case basis.
Speaking at the seminar, Mr. Servio Samudio, former Ambassador of Panama to Vietnam, noted that Vietnam is a strong manufacturing country, while Panama is a connecting hub of the Americas, and the two economies complement each other. According to him, the relationship between the two countries is at a favorable point for promoting cooperation, and the long-term foundation of this relationship is the strong people-to-people connection.
The seminar was held immediately after the visit of the President of Panama to Vietnam, contributing to the concretization of commitments between the leaders of the two countries and opening up many opportunities for cooperation in trade, investment, and logistics between Vietnamese and Panamanian businesses.
